thread:
maria: Kicking off design thread for AWS KMS integration for Redwood Private (VPC). We need a clear envelope flow, RBAC model, audit logging requirements, rotation cadence, and incident runbooks. Initial reactions?

 dave: Two onboarding patterns to support: 1) customer-owned CMK with key policy grants to our service role; 2) assume-role into a customer account and call KMS with temporary creds. Both have pros/cons (UX vs least privilege).

 erin: For self-serve, key-policy grants are simpler. For enterprise/BYOK/HSM we'll prefer assume-role. Also want to surface alias conventions in Console and Terraform snippets.

 sam: DEK caching: nodes will only keep DEKs in memory, default TTL 15m configurable. On rotation we should rewrap cached DEKs where possible; if compromised, treat all DEKs as rewrap candidates.

 maria: Envelope model proposal: GenerateDataKey using customer CMK -> use DEK to encrypt payload -> store ciphertext and minimal metadata (wrapped_by, wrap_ts, actor, trace_id). Never persist plaintext DEKs.

 erin: Rewrap worker: idempotent, resumable, sharded per-customer. It should pick up envelopes with older wrap_arn and call ReEncrypt to new CMK, then update metadata and emit an audit event linking to CloudTrail. Must be safe for node restarts.

 dave: Rewrap rollout plan: 1) create new CMK alias alias/redwood/priv/data/<acct>-<region>-v2 2) new writes use v2 3) start background rewrap workers 4) keep old CMK enabled for a configurable grace period (default 7d). Edgecases: partial progress, node restarts, and throttling.

 sam: KMS rate limits are real. Worker must implement batching, exponential backoff, per-account rate caps, and a circuit-breaker so we don't slam KMS during a mass migration. Add jitter.

 maria: Incident playbook (key compromise): If compromise confirmed: disable compromised CMK (warning: breaks decrypts) -> enable pre-provisioned emergency CMK -> rewrap all DEKs to emergency CMK with high-priority workers and throttling -> once customer provides replacement CMK, rewrap again to new CMK. If only suspected, restrict GenerateDataKey and investigate.

 erin: Storage metadata we should add: wrapped_by (ARN), wrap_ts (ISO8601), wrap_version, wrap_actor, wrap_trace_id. Each rewrap should write a new metadata row and emit an audit log entry with the worker id and CloudTrail request id.

 dave: IAM patterns documented for onboarding: example key policy granting arn:aws:iam::REPO_ACCOUNT:role/redwood-service-role kms:Encrypt kms:Decrypt kms:ReEncrypt* kms:GenerateDataKey* for self-serve. For enterprise recommend assume-role named redwood-onboard-role and grant sts:AssumeRole to our principal.

 maria: RBAC in Console: customer_admin can upload/rotate their CMK alias and view audit logs; redwood_ops can trigger emergency rewrap but only with JIT two-person approval; support_readonly can view rewrap status and metrics. No ops changes to customer key policy allowed.

 sam: Audit logging requirements: enable CloudTrail data events for KMS. Centralize these logs to our observability pipeline with 365d retention. Correlate each Encrypt/Decrypt/ReEncrypt call to our request-id and envelope id for traceability.

 erin: Example onboarding key policy we'll include in docs (snippet):
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "RedwoodServiceAccess",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REPO_ACCOUNT:role/redwood-service-role"},
      "Action": ["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:ReEncrypt*","kms:GenerateDataKey*"],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```

 maria: Rotation cadence proposals: CMK rotate annually by default (customer can override); DEKs rewrap every 30 days or at major platform bumps; cache TTL 15m default.

 dave: Metrics and alerts: export rewrap_rate, rewrap_failures, pending_envelopes, last_rewrap_ts_per_customer. Alert if rewrap_failures > 0 for 30m or pending_envelopes exceeds threshold 6h. Dashboard per-customer.

 sam: Vulnerability triage: if a node memory leak exposes plaintext DEKs, we must treat all ciphertext that used those DEKs as suspect. Triage steps: identify scope (node IDs, timeframe) -> rotate affected DEKs -> optionally rotate dataset-level keys -> notify customer and run postmortem.

 erin: Console UX: show current CMK alias, last rotation, rewrap progress bar, pending counts, and exportable CSV of rewrap events (with wrap_trace_id and CloudTrail id).

 maria: Soft-delete policy: require PendingWindow >= 30 days for CMK deletes. If a customer requests immediate purge, escalate to compliance; do not auto-purge.

 dave: Control-plane vs dataplane: absolutely separate CMKs. Use alias patterns: alias/redwood/priv/ctrl/<acct> and alias/redwood/priv/data/<acct>-<region>. Avoid reusing keys across planes.

 sam: Pre-provision an emergency CMK per-customer during onboarding (kept disabled) so emergency rewrap can be faster. But ensure that emergency key is governed by strict access controls.

 maria: Next steps: Erin -> draft onboarding doc, TF examples, Console fields. Dave -> prototype assume-role automation and key-grant flow, plus a demo rewrap job. Sam -> implement rewrap worker spec, backoff rules, and incident runbook. I'll produce RBAC matrix and escalation steps.

 sec-bot: Reminder: enable CloudTrail data events for KMS and S3; set centralized log retention to 365d.

 deploy-bot: queued change: ops/kms/onboard -> branch: kms-proxy-onboard-2765432101

 sam: Adding tasks to sec-ops sprint. Thanks all.
